hero.name: Takahiro Saeki
hero.description: Frontend development centered on React / TypeScript / Next.js. I love building things and creating animation-driven experiences.

items.title: Haine · The Soul Ledger
items.description: A dark fantasy adventure about Haine, a gray-cat witch reclaiming stolen souls. Combine a 5×5 bingo board with turn-based card battles, completing lines to gain power, block, and mana. In development for Bezi Mega Jam 2026, with an early browser build available in English and Japanese.

items.title: AIとGame Jamで、ゲームを完成させた話
items.description: A lightning talk on finishing and publishing VOLT NOMAD for AI Browser Game Jam 4. Covers prototyping, Godot development, Codex, PixelLab, Suno, and the playtesting and selection process behind the finished game. Published August 27, 2026. Slides in Japanese.

items.title: First Light
items.description: A horizontal shooter roguelike about a tiny spark seeking the first dawn. Collect light, choose from nine upgrades, and push back the growing Dark. Created in 48 hours for Nimble Game Jam 2026. A run takes about 5–7 minutes, with English and Japanese support.

items.title: NO HEROES LEFT
items.description: A vertical bullet-hell roguelite set after the villain wins. Choose one of three dark-fleet craft with distinct weapons, steal enemy cores and relics, and evolve through five sectors. Created for Week Sauce, playable in the browser with support for five languages.

items.title: PRIMAL COUNTDOWN
items.description: A prehistoric action roguelite: survive a 90-second dinosaur onslaught, then escape an unbeatable T-Rex to reach a cave. Combine automatic attacks with six adaptations in a roughly two-minute run. Created for Micro Jam 063, with English, Japanese, and gamepad support.

items.title: Voices Diary
items.description: An app to record and visualize your vocal training practice. Log your practice time, voice condition, and notes, and stay consistent with streaks and a heatmap. Supports tagging reference videos and syncs data between the web app and iOS app.

items.title: SquadNote
items.description: An app that simplifies running a club: schedule creation, one-tap attendance, invite-link joining, and monthly LINE sharing. Completely free with no ads.

items.title: VOLT NOMAD
items.description: A compact incremental boss rush about a recovery automaton descending into a subterranean world engine. Generate CHARGE with manual attacks, then strengthen your build through five gear trees and the cores of defeated machine beasts. Built with Godot 4.6, playable in English or Japanese in the browser.

items.title: Roll for Six
items.description: An incremental clicker game where you roll six dice and keep matching sixes to progress. Features skill unlocks, boss battles, and an infinite mode, with full content playable in 60-90 minutes. Built with Godot Engine 4.x.

items.title: LOOP HAXE
items.description: A hack-and-slash roguelike where you watch a horde of summoned beasts fight automatically. Choose your path through branching dungeons and build synergies from relics, beasts, and skills. A browser-playable game built with Godot.

categories.title: Frameworks
categories.note: React is my strong suit. I often use react-redux for state management.

categories.title: Build Tools
categories.note: I choose tools by use case: webpack at work, and webpack or parcel for personal projects.

categories.title: Design Tools
categories.note: I mostly use Figma at work, and Photoshop for personal projects.

categories.title: CSS
categories.note: In React environments I mostly use styled-components, so it's mostly CSS-in-JS, but personally I prefer PostCSS.

categories.title: AI
categories.note: I use AI-assisted development daily, centered on Claude Code. For my personal game projects, I also leverage AI for code generation and sound production.

categories.title: Others
categories.note: In my private time I've enjoyed using web components and following the spec. I get to use them occasionally at work too, and I'd like to use them more proactively.

items.title: Born into this world
items.desc: After finishing high school entrance exams, I spent years in band life, focused on composing and playing live.

items.title: Became a freelance engineer

items.title: Renewal of an online reservation system
items.desc: Development using an in-house JavaScript framework. This work led me to start learning ECMAScript 2015.

items.title: SNS app development
items.desc: Mainly worked on implementing JavaScript animations.

items.title: Language study in Vancouver
items.desc: Studied English in Canada while attending meetups almost every week, connecting with local engineers. Through my hobby DanceDanceRevolution, I made 20-30 friends in the Vancouver DDR community.

items.title: Frontend work for an e-book service
items.desc: After returning to Japan, I focused on frontend implementation to improve an e-book service at a company. I also hosted weekly in-house study sessions, helping raise the team's frontend skills.

items.title: Togetter
